summary: This CSS defines a scroll-to-top button that's hidden by default, appears when the user scrolls down, and animates smoothly when clicked. The button scales up slightly on hover and flies upward with a shrinking effect when activated, with responsive sizing for mobile devices.

explanations.2: position: fixed means the button stays in the same spot on screen even when you scroll, rather than moving with the page content.
explanations.8: opacity: 0 makes the button completely transparent (invisible) from the start.
explanations.9: visibility: hidden hides the button entirely so it doesn't take up space or respond to clicks, even though it's technically there.
explanations.10: The transition lines tell the browser to smoothly animate changes to opacity and visibility over 0.4 seconds instead of switching instantly.
explanations.13: z-index: 1000 stacks this button on top of almost everything else on the page so it's always clickable.
explanations.22: object-fit: contain makes the image inside the button scale proportionally to fit without getting squished or cut off.
explanations.33: When JavaScript adds the 'show' class to the button, these rules make it fade in and become clickable.
explanations.40: This applies the flyUp animation to the image inside the button when the 'fly' class is added, making it play once over 0.8 seconds.
explanations.45: translateY(0) means the image starts at its normal vertical position, and scale(1) means it's at full size.
explanations.49: translateY(-300px) moves the image up 300 pixels, and scale(0.6) shrinks it to 60% of its original size during the animation.
